title: Exec ambient brief and open-floor format (Q3 prep v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working brief for the exec update + all-team open-floor session we want to run the week of June 16 (Q3 kickoff cadence). Goal: create an "ambient" all-hands where macro context is set quickly, execs cover clarifying decisions (not long readouts), and most time is reserved for cross-team questions and short breakout commitments.

Audience:
- All employees (engineering, product, go-to-market, support, SRE, applied ML).
- Optional smaller parallel session for partners/customer advocates.

TL;DR (for slack blurbs):
- 45min company update (15m exec highlights, 25m open-floor Q&A, 5m closing asks)
- Focus: 1) what we’re committing to this quarter (top 3 bets), 2) what success looks like (leading metrics), 3) where we need cross-team help.

Run of Show (proposed) — strict timings:
- 0:00–0:02 Host welcome + safety (ops contact + Slack etiquette)
- 0:02–0:12 CEO framing: market + strategic implications (10m) — 3 slides max
- 0:12–0:17 Product highlight (hosted + dedicated progress; 5m) — one rapid demo or screenshot
- 0:17–0:22 Engineering highlight (serving runtime, reliability; 5m) — 1 metric callout
- 0:22–0:27 GTM & sales: buyer momentum + enterprise signals (5m)
- 0:27–0:52 Open-floor (25m): live questions via Slido + curated table (see mechanics)
- 0:52–0:55 Closing asks (3 team-anchored commitments) + where to find follow-ups

Why this shape?
- Short exec signals keep attention and reduce slide-drift.
- Open-floor incentivizes transparency and surfaces cross-team blockers early.
- Closing asks convert alignment into immediate actions.

OKR snapshot (draft language — please edit inline):
- Northstar: reduce average end-to-end inference cost per 1k tokens by 18% while keeping median P50 latency within SLA.
  - Key results: reduce per-token infra cost (GPU amortized) by 12–15% (model + quantization changes), increase cache hit rate to 22%, and automate 2 rollout playbooks to reduce failed deploy rollback time by 60%.
- Developer adoption: onboard 3 new enterprise customers to Dedicated by EoQ with baseline SLAs verified.
- Reliability: reach 99.95% platform uptime for hosted API across primary regions.

Quick metrics to show (single slide):
- Weekly tokens served (trend last 12 weeks) — annotate 2 spikes with root causes
- P50 latency (overall and for top 3 models)
- Cost per 1k tokens (rolling) + delta vs prior quarter
- Dedicated capacity utilization (% of committed capacity)

Open-floor mechanics (how to run cleanly):
- Use Slido for question submission + upvote. Run moderator queue in parallel (Ops + comms).
- Live chat (Slack #company-all) should be for clarifying links only; all substantive asks must be submitted to Slido or the facilitator.
- Moderator handoff: moderator reads top 3 Slido questions, routes to the right panelist. If a question requires a follow-up, capture in the "follow-up tracker" (JIRA ops ticket template below).

Speaker assignments (draft):
- Host / Moderator: Maya Patel (ops) — open, timekeeping, Slido queue manager.
- CEO: Arun Sinha — strategic framing.
- VP Product: Claire Ng — product bets + quick demo.
- CTO: Ethan Brooks — runtime optimizations + reliability.
- VP GTM: Sasha Rivera — customer momentum + enterprise asks.

Closing asks (three) — these should be short, actionable, and assigned:
1) Engineering: finalize quantization rollout plan for model family X (owner: Ethan) — deliverable: rollout playbook + canary policy by June 30 (JIRA: INF-733).
2) Sales & Solutions: confirm 3 Dedicated onboarding pipelines and point-of-contact for each (owner: Sasha) — deliverable: list + deployment windows by June 25 (JIRA: GTM-198).
3) Customer Success & Product: compile 5 representative prompt sets for quality monitoring regression alerts (owner: Claire) — deliverable: dataset + threshold proposals by June 28 (JIRA: CS-441).

Prep checklist (two-week timeline):
- Week -2 (now): finalize run of show, slide decks (CEO + 3 execs), Slido setup, 2 rehearsals scheduled. Owner: Maya.
- Week -1: Exec rehearsal #1 (wet run, 30m), capture slide edits.
- Days -3 and -1: Tech check (AV, streaming, captions), confirm backup presenters.
- Day 0: Final rehearsal (15m), publish slack invite + pre-read doc (short one-pager — this doc condensed).

Rehearsal playbook (what to practice):
- “Start strong” 15-second line: each speaker prepares one concise framing sentence to set context.
- Transition handoffs: who speaks next and one-sentence bridge.
- One real ask: each exec must end their segment with a single ask for specific teams.

Accessibility & recording:
- Live captions on. Record session and auto-publish to company drive (ops will clip the 3 asks into a 90-second recap).

Fallbacks and contingency (short-form):
- If streaming fails: end early + post the 12-minute exec video in Drive + extend open-floor to next day as a townline thread.
- If CEO unavailable: CTO covers strategic frame and CEO recorded intro is played.

Follow-up process (tidy):
- All follow-up actions get a JIRA ticket in the "All Hands Follow-ups" board with owners and due dates. Ops will triage and ensure owners acknowledge within 48 hours.
- A 2-week status checkpoint (asynchronous) will be published as a one-slide update in the #company-all channel.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self and execs):
- Do we want to run a 10-min vertical-breakout after the 25m open-floor for product/solutions teams? Pros: targeted signal; cons: splits attention. Need exec opinion by May 19.
- Who curates the “top issues” list for the open-floor — ops or the execs? Default: ops to curate but execs can flag 1 question to bump.
- Should we invite 2–3 enterprise customers to watch live? Risk: live questions from customers could derail candidness. Suggest recorded segment with Q&A via SEs only.

Draft Slack announcement (to be edited and scheduled):
"Heads up — Company Update + Open Floor, Mon Jun 16 10:00–10:45 PT. Quick 15m exec framing, 25m live Q&A (submit/vote via Slido), 5m closing asks. Pre-read: one pager with top metrics (coming Fri). We’ll record and publish. Please use #company-all for clarifying links only. — Maya"

Action items (immediate):
- Maya: finalize Slido + create follow-up JIRA board (due 2025-05-14).
- Ethan: draft quantization rollout bullet points for one slide (due 2025-05-19).
- Claire: assemble 3 demo screenshots + short script (due 2025-05-19).
- Sasha: compile enterprise onboarding candidate list (due 2025-05-21).

Notes to self: keep deck to 6 slides total; avoid slide-dump. Use 1 metric per slide.

End of working draft — please comment inline.
